status: PRE-REGISTERED — written before the candidate stack existed
param: stack route within the undistort class

control.shape: 500 frames -> one register -2pass -> -framing=min -> stack rej g 0.3 0.05

candidate.shape: 5 groups x 100 -> per-group register+stack rej g 0.3 0.05 -> register sub-stacks -> compose PLAIN MEAN

hypothesis: The groups route costs nothing measurable on this data. The repo has carried 'one extra interpolation pass' as a DECLARED cost since the route was written and has never measured it.
not_one_knob_and_that_is_stated_up_front: The arms differ in TWO things: the extra interpolation pass, AND the rejection denominator (one GESD over 500 vs five GESD over 100 then a plain-mean compose). A NULL clears both together. A non-null does NOT attribute itself between them.

pre_registered_thresholds.why: Pre-committing the threshold that would TRIGGER a third arm is cheaper than designing the third arm now, and it stops the threshold being chosen after the numbers are visible.

flux_same_arm_repeat_floor.source: docs/dead-ends.md — measured on THIS chain, two runs, identical recipe
flux_same_arm_repeat_floor.rule: any difference at or below these is UNMEASURED, per the registry's own wording

shape_instrument_bounds.source: incumbent-vs-x86-refit A/B — two genuinely DIFFERENT optical models, everything else identical. These are an UPPER BOUND on instrument noise, not a measured repeat floor: the arms differed by a real sub-pixel model change.
shape_instrument_bounds.rule: differences below these are certainly not resolvable by these instruments here

pre_registered_thresholds.decision: ALL measures within the floors -> NULL, the declared cost is a measured null, the route is cheap forever, NO third arm. ANY measure above its floor -> the two-variable confound is live and a third arm is required to split interpolation from rejection denominator.

scope_limit: set-01 is the WEAKEST set for the rejection-denominator term: its 7 setup frames are already culled and the known aircraft is in set-03. So a null here is closer to a clean interpolation result than the two-variable framing implies — and set-03 is the informative follow-up, because it holds the transient the rejection is supposed to catch AND the route-conditional ratified keep.
